## Executive summary

Routine KPI tracking showed me an opportunity to understand a promotion better, so I started a structured diagnostic on my own initiative. I then worked with stakeholders to turn what I found into product and go-to-market recommendations.

## Business challenge

An advertising promotion presented an opportunity to improve commercial performance through more structured measurement and customer understanding.

## My role

- Spotted the opportunity through cross-channel KPI tracking and took on the analysis without a formal mandate
- Analyzed sales results across customer segments, sales channels, and promotional periods (Excel, Tableau)
- Developed product and go-to-market recommendations
- Partnered with cross-functional stakeholders to refine the plan and build buy-in

## Analytical approach

I initiated a performance diagnostic, compared results across customer segments and promotional periods, and translated findings into recommendations. I treated each possible explanation as a hypothesis to test, so that the evidence decided the next step.

## Illustrative decision framework

**How I structure a promotion diagnostic**

[Illustrative framework]{.provenance .provenance-illustrative}

| Hypothesis considered | Evidence required | Potential action |
|---|---|---|
| **Audience fit:** is the offer reaching the right customers? | Adoption by customer segment | Refine who the offer targets |
| **Offer design:** is the incentive relevant to each group? | Response across offer types and segments | Adjust the structure of the offer |
| **Timing:** does the window match when customers plan and spend? | Results across periods and buying cycles | Change when the promotion runs |
| **Channel execution:** is the offer being sold consistently? | Performance across sales channels | Improve enablement or channel focus |

[Illustrative decision framework: hypotheses a diagnostic could consider, not confirmed findings. It does not describe LINE's actual campaigns, rules, or results.]{.illustrative}

## Outcome

- Recommendations informed improvements to promotional execution and contributed to stronger sales performance
- The work showed how cross-channel KPI tracking can surface questions that are hard to see from inside a single team

## Lessons learned

- **Test the obvious explanation.** Writing down competing hypotheses keeps a diagnostic from stopping at the first plausible answer.
- **Look at several lenses together.** Segment, offer, and timing can explain more in combination than any one view does alone.
- **Frame findings as iteration.** Recommendations are easier to act on when they build on a team's work rather than critique it.
